mil3.1.14:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of immersion?”
mil3.1.14:1.3: “Immersion, Great King, has the characteristic of being foremost: whatever skillful qualities there are, all of them have immersion foremost, slant to immersion, slope to immersion, and incline to immersion.”
mil3.1.14:2.2: “Just as, Great King, of whatever rafters there are in a house with a peaked roof, all of them lead to the peak, slant to the peak, and meet at the peak, and the peak is called the chief of them;
mil3.1.14:2.3: so too, Great King, whatever skillful qualities there are, all of them have immersion foremost, slant to immersion, slope to immersion, and incline to immersion.”
mil3.1.14:3.2: “Just as, Great King, if some king were to go into battle with an army of four divisions, the entire army—elephants, horses, chariots, and foot soldiers—would have him as its foremost, slant to him, slope to him, incline to him, and would revolve around him alone;
mil3.1.14:3.3: so too, Great King, whatever skillful qualities there are, all of them have immersion foremost, slant to immersion, slope to immersion, and incline to immersion.
mil3.1.14:3.4: That, Great King, is how immersion has the characteristic of being foremost.
mil3.1.14:3.6: ‘Develop immersion, mendicants; a mendicant who is immersed understands things as they really are.’”
